name: Winter Pavilion
tagline: A pink deco pavilion alone in a photographed snowfield, and a sun you can drag down into night.
summary: A matte painting built from real CC0 photographs and a rendered pavilion: one building, one sun, a great deal of sky. Dragging the sun relights the scene through low winter sun, pink hour and blue night, and that sunset is also the site's day-to-night switch. The products are small pastel buildings in the same snow, each carrying its real sign, so a growing company simply adds houses to the street.
voice: Deadpan, exact and understated, like a well-made sign: 'Software that keeps its own lights on.'
motion: Slow and frontal: a camera that dollies sideways past the facades, layers that drift by depth, and an iris that opens night from the switch.
sound: Off until asked; then a soft two-note sine chime, rising when the day comes back and falling when the sign switches on.
mark: An arched window with the sun sitting on its horizon over three snow lines, next to ALBRETSEN in Jost capitals spaced like a rooftop sign.
